name: Cha ruoi
summary: Chả rươi is a seasonal fried ragworm cake, and the accounts do not match. Cổng thông tin điện tử thành phố Hải Phòng, on 16 October 2025, names it as a dish of the former Hải Dương land now inside the city and does not give a recipe. TITC, on the rural-tourism site, says the worm is taken mainly in Tiên Lãng and Vĩnh Bảo. Ủy ban nhân dân phường Hồng Bàng, on 1 September 2025, writes of rươi from Tứ Kỳ.
origin: Hai Phong. Three accounts name different grounds: former Hải Dương, Tiên Lãng and Vĩnh Bảo, and Tứ Kỳ.
texture: TITC says the fried cake is slightly charred and crisp outside, and soft and fatty inside. That page does not print a date.
taste: TITC says the mix is cleaned ragworm pounded with minced pork, egg, dill, and shredded tangerine peel, and calls the tangerine peel the mark of the taste.
howToEat: TITC says dip it in sweet-sour fish sauce and eat it with herbs and rice noodles, or with the red crackers. It says the worm runs in lunar months 9 and 10, and that people eat the cake in the early morning and the late afternoon in that season.
The 16 October 2025 account does not print a season. A price was not printed. The hour is Check on arrival.
where: TITC names Lê Chân, Ngô Quyền, and the markets Lương Văn Can and Cầu Đất. The 16 October 2025 account names the former Hải Dương side and no port street. Phường Hồng Bàng names Tứ Kỳ. All three stay. The hour is Check on arrival.
seoTitle: Cha ruoi — Hai Phong’s seasonal ragworm cake
seoDescription: Fried ragworm with pork, egg, dill, and tangerine peel on the TITC account. Other accounts name former Hải Dương and Tứ Kỳ. A price is Check on arrival.
